rationale: All 8 prior blocking findings were graded resolved against current source: doctor-groups.js now carries the collapsed runtime row and multi-failure joins through remedyFor() (CR-001/CR-002, matching new tests); health-ui.js's showLogError recreates the wiped error banner (CR-003); the runHealthCheck wiring was extracted into a new ui/health-controller.js (imported by renderer.js, which is in changed_files) that adds a running-guard (CR-004), an explicit could-not-determine state for zero stdout records (CR-005), a try/catch around runStream with onFailure resetting renderer.js's healthChecked one-shot guard (CR-006), and a real end-to-end pipeline test plus an open_log-rejection test (CR-007/CR-008), all verified by reading health-controller.js, doctor-groups.js, health-ui.js and renderer.js directly rather than trusting fix_evidence's self-reported status. Note: health-controller.js and ui/test/health-controller.test.mjs (new files carrying the CR-004..CR-008 fixes) were absent from the supplied changed_files list, likely because a diff-against-HEAD computation misses new untracked files; renderer.js's import of createHealthController (itself in changed_files) confirmed the wiring is genuine, so this did not block verification. business_review and standards_review are carried forward unchanged from the prior verdict per contract.

findings.title: Failed runtime check has no remedy
findings.problem: The collapsed Node/Npm/Python/Uv row is pushed with only {group, label, status} — unlike per-check rows it is never given a remedyText or action, even when worst(runtime) resolves to 'fail'.
findings.impact: A user sees a red 'Everything CodeMie needs to run is included' row with zero indication of which of the four runtime checks failed or what to do about it, defeating the screen's remedy-per-failure goal for the row group most likely to fail (a missing binary).
findings.recommendation: Find the failing runtime record(s) and its hint the same way per-name rows do, and attach a remedyText/action (e.g. a 'Check again' button when a hint exists) to the collapsed row too.

findings.title: Only the first of multiple failures gets a remedy
findings.problem: `items.find((r) => r.status === 'error' || r.status === 'warn')` picks only the first failing detail line for a check name; a check reporting two distinct failures (e.g. Agents in the fixtures) has its second failure's hint silently absorbed into the aggregate status.
findings.impact: When a check fails for two reasons at once, the row shows 'fail' but only ever surfaces the first cause's remedy — the second failure has no visible hint or action.
findings.recommendation: Use `items.filter(...)` to collect all failing items for the name and join their hints/actions, instead of taking only the first match.

findings.title: Concurrent open-log error can be dropped silently
findings.problem: showLoading(container) unconditionally does `container.innerHTML = ''`, removing the `.health-log-error` element that showLogError looks up. Clicking 'Open today's log' then 'Check everything again' before the first invoke('open_log') settles races showLoading's wipe against the pending rejection's handler.
findings.impact: When the log-open rejection's showLogError callback finally runs after the wipe, querySelector returns null, showLogError returns early, and the log-open failure is reported nowhere — a silent no-op contrary to the spec's 'never a silent no-op' requirement for this path.
findings.recommendation: Give showLogError a fallback path (re-render the error banner independent of the row list), or disable the log button while open_log is pending so it cannot race a recheck.

findings.title: No re-entrancy guard on runHealthCheck
findings.problem: runHealthCheck() has no busy-flag equivalent to the existing `installRunning` pattern; nothing stops 'Check everything again' or a per-row 'Check again' from firing a second `runStream('codemie doctor', ...)` while an earlier one is still in flight.
findings.impact: Two concurrent doctor runs can both eventually call renderHealth(); whichever resolves last overwrites the render regardless of which check is actually current, and a rapid double-click doubles the doctor process load for no benefit.
findings.recommendation: Add a `healthRunning` flag mirroring `installRunning`: return early from runHealthCheck() (and disable the recheck buttons) while a run is already in flight.

findings.title: Empty doctor stdout reads as a false all-clear
findings.problem: runHealthCheck only accumulates lines tagged 'stdout'; if `codemie doctor` exits having written nothing to stdout (its own error output on stderr, or a non-zero exit with no stdout), parseDoctorOutput('') returns no records and groupDoctorResults returns rows: [] with summary {passing:0, total:0}.
findings.impact: The Health screen renders '0 of 0 fine' — visually indistinguishable from a genuine all-clear — silently masking a total failure to run any health check at all.
findings.recommendation: When the run resolves with zero records, render an explicit 'could not determine health' state instead of falling through to the normal 0/0 summary.

findings.title: Doctor run failure leaves Health screen stuck forever
findings.problem: runHealthCheck() has no try/catch around `await bridge.runner.runStream('codemie doctor', ...)`. If the doctor process fails to spawn or run_stream's invoke rejects, the await throws and renderHealth() — which draws the 'Check everything again' button — never runs. The sidebar click handler had already set `healthChecked = true` before calling runHealthCheck(), so the one-time auto-run guard also blocks any later automatic retry.
findings.impact: The Health view is left showing showLoading()'s 'Checking…' text permanently: no error is shown, no recheck button is ever rendered, and re-clicking the sidebar's Health entry does nothing because healthChecked is already true — the only way out is restarting the app.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the runStream call in try/catch; on failure render an explicit error state with a working retry action, and don't let a failed run permanently consume the one-shot healthChecked guard.

findings.title: Doctor pipeline has no end-to-end test
findings.problem: The wiring inside runHealthCheck — the stdout-tag filter, `lines.join('\n')`, and the handoff into parseDoctorOutput/groupDoctorResults — has no test exercising the actual call chain; doctor-parse.test.mjs and doctor-groups.test.mjs both call the two pure functions directly with hand-built fixtures/records.
findings.impact: If the stdout-tag filter were inverted or the join/parse hookup broken, the Health screen would render on the doctor's own prompt echo or stderr noise instead of real results (or render nothing) — and both existing test files would keep passing, giving false confidence around exactly the class of gap found in CR-006.
findings.recommendation: Add a test that stubs bridge.runner.runStream to emit mixed-tag lines and asserts the resulting render reflects only the stdout-derived records, exercising runHealthCheck's real call chain.

findings.title: Open-log failure path has no test
findings.problem: The wiring that surfaces an open_log rejection through showLogError (renderer.js's onOpenLog catch block) is untested, and showLogError itself has no direct unit test; health-ui.test.mjs's three tests only cover renderHealth's rows/summary/buttons.
findings.impact: If the catch block were dropped, or showLogError's '.health-log-error' selector drifted from the class name renderHealth actually renders, a failed log-open (now reachable since open_log can reject via ensure_log_readable) would fail silently with no user-visible message, and no test would catch it.
findings.recommendation: Add a test that stubs invoke('open_log') to reject and asserts showLogError is invoked with a message, plus a direct unit test of showLogError(container, msg) asserting it unhides '.health-log-error' and sets its text.

finding_status.notes: doctor-groups.js's collapsed runtime row now runs through remedyFor(runtime, status, undefined) and gets remedyText/action on failure; verified against source and the new CR-001 test.
remedyFor() filters all failing items (not .find's first match) and joins unique hints with '\n'; verified against source and the new CR-002 test covering two distinct Agents failures.

showLogError() now looks up '.health-log-error' and recreates it via appendChild when absent, instead of returning early; verified against source and the new CR-003 test simulating a wipe-then-error race.

runHealthCheck was extracted into ui/health-controller.js's createHealthController().run(), which sets a `running` flag and returns immediately if already running (finally clears it); verified against source and two CR-004/health-controller.test.mjs tests.

run() checks `records.length === 0` and calls showRunError() with a could-not-determine message and retry action instead of falling through to renderHealth's 0/0; verified against source and the CR-005 test.

run() wraps runStream in try/catch; the catch renders showRunError() with a working retry and calls onFailure(), which renderer.js wires to reset healthChecked so the one-shot guard is not permanently stuck; verified against source (renderer.js + health-controller.js) and two CR-006 tests.

The stdout-tag filter/join/parse/group/render pipeline now lives in one function (run()) covered by a test that stubs runStream with mixed prompt/stdout/stderr-tagged lines and asserts only stdout-derived output renders; verified the runner-bridge.js onLine(text, tag) signature matches what the test stub and run() both assume.

handleOpenLog()'s catch now calls showLogError with a formatted message; covered by a CR-008 test stubbing a rejecting openLog and asserting the message renders via the real Open today's log button click.
